title: 5c PRD: convention system design
description:
## Problem Statement

Sutra's convention system (Layer 2) currently detects patterns via FCA and stores lifecycle overrides, but lacks the full machinery needed to serve as a living convention system for human-AI teams. Agents get no structural guidance on what patterns to follow when writing new code. Convention drift across agent sessions goes undetected. The human has no propose-and-confirm workflow for managing convention lifecycle — promotion and demotion are manual and disconnected from trend data. There is no audit trail for intentional deviations from conventions.

## Solution

A complete convention system that discovers patterns at two levels (global and per-component), tracks their health over time, proposes lifecycle transitions to the human, generates structural templates for agent orientation, detects drift via attribute entropy, and maintains a waiver audit trail — all while keeping conventions strictly advisory (enforcement is Layer 3 constraints).

## User Stories

1. As an agent, I want to receive preferred conventions with signature templates when oriented to a component, so that I write code that follows the component's established patterns.
2. As an agent, I want to be warned about deprecated and forbidden conventions during orientation, so that I avoid copying anti-patterns.
3. As an architect, I want conventions discovered both globally and per-component, so that I can see both cross-cutting patterns and local ones.
4. As an architect, I want sutra to propose convention promotions when a descriptive pattern stabilizes (high support/confidence across multiple snapshots), so that I don't have to manually monitor every convention.
5. As an architect, I want sutra to propose deprecation when a preferred convention's support is declining, so that I can acknowledge codebase evolution rather than fighting it.
6. As an architect, I want to accept or dismiss lifecycle proposals, so that I remain in control of which conventions are enforced.
7. As an architect, I want dismissed proposals to not re-trigger unless the underlying signal changes direction, so that I'm not nagged.
8. As an architect, I want convention violations to be advisory (never blocking), so that conventions inform and warn without gate-keeping merges — that's what constraints are for.
9. As an architect, I want to waive a specific convention violation with rationale, so that the review report shows which deviations are intentional vs unnoticed.
10. As an architect, I want waivers to appear in every review report that touches the waived area, so that I can audit the accumulation of deviations over time.
11. As an architect, I want orphaned waivers (whose convention ID changed after FCA recompute) surfaced in reconciliation, so that I can decide whether to transfer or discard them.
12. As an architect, I want to see attribute entropy trends per component, so that I can detect convention drift before any single convention formally breaks.
13. As an architect, I want drift alerts suppressed for components in sketch mode, so that intentional exploration doesn't trigger false alarms.
14. As an architect, I want drift reports to tell me which attributes are diverging (not just that entropy is rising), so that I know where the drift is.
15. As an architect, I want structural templates auto-generated from exemplar symbols, so that agents get concrete signature skeletons without me authoring templates manually.
16. As an architect, I want templates to reflect current code (regenerated on FCA rebuild), so that templates don't go stale as the codebase evolves.
17. As an agent, I want the convention check to flag me when I write new or modified code that matches a deprecated/forbidden convention, so that I don't inadvertently adopt anti-patterns.
18. As an agent, I want one-hop effect attributes (fs, net, db, mut_state) included in conventions, so that effect-based patterns like "all functions in this component are pure" are discoverable.
19. As an architect, I want FCA rebuilds skipped when the attribute matrix hasn't changed (hash check), so that rebuild cycles are fast on no-op changes.
20. As an architect, I want per-component FCA to use adaptive support thresholds (proportional to component size, floor of 2), so that small components don't produce spurious conventions and large components require proportionally stronger patterns.
21. As an architect, I want the module renamed from fca/ to conventions/ to reflect its broader purpose, so that the module name matches the concern rather than the substrate.

## Implementation Decisions

### Convention engine
- Two-level FCA: global across all symbols, plus per-component for each component with sufficient symbols.
- Adaptive threshold for per-component FCA: min_support = max(2, ceil(component_symbol_count * 0.4)). Global FCA retains current MIN_SUPPORT=3, MIN_CONFIDENCE=0.9.
- Deduplication: if a component convention is subsumed by a global convention (same implication, equal or higher confidence), drop the component one.
- Optimized full rebuild: hash the attribute matrix (blake3), skip FCA recomputation when hash is unchanged. No true incremental lattice — YAGNI at sutra's scale.
- Conventions carry a nullable component_id. NULL = global, non-null = scoped to that component.

### Lifecycle and propose-and-confirm
- Four lifecycle states: descriptive (default), preferred, deprecated, forbidden. All transitions are human-initiated (via MCP tool) or proposed by sutra and confirmed by human.
- Propose-and-confirm signals: stable high support → propose promote to preferred; declining support on preferred → propose deprecate; zero matching symbols for N snapshots on deprecated → propose deletion; new convention contradicting deprecated → surface as replacement candidate.
- Proposals stored in convention_proposals table (durable). States: pending, accepted, dismissed. Dismissed proposals don't re-trigger unless signal direction reverses.
- Hardcoded thresholds (N=3 consecutive snapshots for trend signals). No user-facing configuration surface.

### Trust model interaction
- Conventions are always advisory regardless of lifecycle state. Lifecycle gates orientation messaging and violation tone, never blocks.
- Descriptive = informational in orient, no violations. Preferred = "follow this" + advisory violations. Deprecated = "avoid this" + advisory warning on new/modified code matching the pattern (inverse check). Forbidden = "anti-pattern" + louder advisory on match.
- Full waiver tracking: convention violations can be waived with rationale. Waivers annotate the finding in reports, they don't suppress it. Waivers reference symbols by qualified name (survives reindex).

### Structural templates
- Auto-generated from exemplar symbols. Exemplars ranked by: attribute coverage beyond convention minimum, median complexity, recency.
- Signature-level skeletons for v1 (visibility through return type). Body structure deferred.
- Extracted via tree-sitter. Output is a parameterized signature string with metavariables for varying parts.
- Templates stored in ephemeral convention_templates table (recomputable). No human authoring — influence via writing exemplary code and promoting conventions.
- Served in orientation responses alongside preferred conventions.

### Effect tracking
- One-hop effect detection: after normal attribute extraction, look up outgoing calls edges and match callee qualified names against per-adapter effect pattern lists.
- Effect attributes: effect:fs, effect:net, effect:db, effect:mut_state, effect:unsafe_transitive.
- Pattern lists hardcoded per adapter (known std lib / common crate patterns). No user configuration for v1.
- Effect attributes enter the FCA matrix as regular attributes, enabling effect-based convention discovery.

### Drift detection
- Attribute distribution entropy (Shannon) per component per FCA snapshot.
- Stored in convention_snapshots table (ephemeral, append-only).
- Drift alert when entropy increases by > 0.15 over 3 consecutive snapshots.
- Drift reports include which attributes are diverging (proportion moving toward 0.5).
- Suppressed for components in sketch mode (ADR-0001).
- Surfaces in review reports and as a health metric.

### Storage evolution
- convention_overrides renamed to convention_state, extended with component scope.
- New durable tables: convention_waivers, convention_proposals.
- New ephemeral tables: convention_templates, convention_snapshots.
- Migration path is incremental — rename + add columns first, new tables as features land.

### Module rename
- src/fca/ → src/conventions/ in the first PR, before new code lands. Single commit: move files, update mod.rs and imports. Engine internals unchanged in that commit.

## Testing Decisions

Good tests verify external behavior through the module's public interface — not implementation details like internal data structures or private helper functions.

Modules with dedicated tests:

- conventions/engine.rs — extend existing FCA engine tests for: per-component FCA dispatch, adaptive threshold behavior (verify small components use proportional support, floor of 2), deduplication of component conventions subsumed by global ones, attribute matrix hash caching (verify rebuild is skipped on unchanged input). Prior art: existing fca/engine.rs tests.
- conventions/templates.rs — test exemplar selection (correct ranking by coverage/complexity/recency), signature skeleton extraction (parameterized output from known Rust functions), metavariable substitution. Test via constructed SymbolAttrs + tree-sitter parsed source.
- conventions/drift.rs — test entropy computation (known distributions → expected entropy values), trend detection (increasing entropy across snapshots triggers alert, flat/decreasing does not), sketch mode suppression. Pure computation — easy to test with synthetic data.
- conventions/lifecycle.rs — test proposal generation from snapshot sequences (rising support → promote proposal, declining → deprecate proposal), dismissal persistence (dismissed proposals don't re-trigger), signal reversal (dismissed proposal re-triggers when signal flips). State machine tests with synthetic convention histories.

## Out of Scope

- Body-level structural templates (beyond signatures) — future enrichment
- Full transitive effect analysis — one-hop is sufficient for now
- True incremental FCA lattice update algorithms — YAGNI at sutra's scale
- User-configurable propose-and-confirm thresholds — hardcoded defaults only
- Human-authored templates — influence via exemplary code instead
- Convention blocking severity — conventions are always advisory; blocking is Layer 3 (constraints)
- Integration with Layer 3 constraint system — separate capability PRD (5d)
- Cross-component convention interaction (convention in A implies convention in B) — complexity not justified yet

## Further Notes

This PRD follows from the brainstorm in sutra/41. Key prior decisions from Phase 5a that this builds on: ADR-0001 (sketch mode relaxes conventions only), ADR-0002 (ephemeral/durable storage partition), ADR-0003 (layered adapter traits with FcaAttributeSource). The convention_overrides durable companion pattern from 5a is the seed that this system grows from.
